cards.headline: Body of murder suspect found after Vero Beach library double killing and ocean escape
cards.body:

The suspect escaped into the Atlantic Ocean following the double homicide at the library, prompting an extensive search by law enforcement and marine units.

The incident began when the suspect opened fire inside the Vero Beach library, killing his wife and another man. Witnesses reported the violent confrontation before the suspect fled the scene and entered the ocean in an apparent attempt to evade capture. Multiple law enforcement agencies responded to the shooting and launched a coordinated search effort along the coastline.

Search teams scoured the waters and shoreline in the hours following the shooting. The suspect's body was later located in the ocean, bringing the manhunt to a conclusion. Authorities have not released the names of the suspect or the victims pending notification of family members.

The library shooting has shaken the Vero Beach community, where such violent incidents are rare. The investigation into the double homicide continues as detectives work to determine the full circumstances surrounding the killings and what motivated the attack. The library remained closed following the incident as investigators processed the crime scene. Authorities have not announced when the facility will reopen to the public.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie woman faces attempted murder charges after setting fire while victim trapped inside bedroom
cards.teaser: A Port St.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie woman faces attempted murder and arson charges after allegedly setting fire to a bedroom door while a 62-year-old woman was inside the room Sunday night. Port St. Lucie Police Department officers responded to reports of a domestic disturbance and active house fire at around 9:05 p.m. in the 1500 block of Southeast Airoso Boulevard. When officers arrived, they found flames inside the residence and immediately worked to evacuate everyone safely.

The investigation revealed that the victim first noticed smoke coming from underneath her bedroom door and discovered Michelle Picard, 26, standing nearby when she opened it. When the victim attempted to retrieve a fire extinguisher, Picard allegedly physically attacked her and tried to prevent her from putting out the fire. Police say Picard made threatening statements and attempted to push the victim toward the flames. The victim managed to escape to a bathroom, lock the door, and call 911. During the emergency call, Picard could be heard banging on the bathroom door in the background.

Officers found Picard outside the residence and detained her. She resisted arrest, causing injuries to one officer's leg and requiring another officer to assist in taking her into custody. Picard faces multiple charges in connection with the incident.

The Port St. Lucie Police Department continues to investigate the case. No additional information about the relationship between Picard and the victim has been released. The incident remains under active investigation as authorities work to determine the full circumstances surrounding the fire and assault.

Authorities arrested the bus driver on charges related to both alleged victims. The second student's allegations prompted investigators to add charges to the case. The driver transported students on routes in St. Lucie County schools before the arrest.

Law enforcement officials confirmed the investigation remains active. Detectives are working to determine if additional students may have been affected. The school district has removed the driver from all duties pending the outcome of the criminal case.

Parents of students who rode the bus driven by the accused individual have been notified by the district. Officials encouraged any families with concerns or information to contact law enforcement. The case highlights ongoing efforts by the school district and sheriff's office to protect students during transportation to and from school.

cards.headline: Property value growth slows for fourth straight year in Florida county
cards.teaser: A Florida county has experienced declining property value growth for four consecutive years, a trend that affects tax revenues and real estate markets.

Property value growth has declined for the fourth consecutive year in a Florida county, marking a sustained slowdown in real estate appreciation. The trend represents a departure from the rapid growth seen in previous years across much of the state.

The four-year decline in property value growth affects county tax revenues, school district funding, and other government services that rely on property tax collections. While property values have not decreased, the rate of increase has slowed each year. This pattern differs from many other Florida counties that have continued to see strong appreciation driven by population growth and housing demand. The slower growth impacts homeowners' equity accumulation and affects real estate market dynamics.

County officials must account for the slower property value growth when budgeting for services and planning capital projects. Property taxes are calculated based on assessed values, so slower appreciation means more modest revenue increases even when tax rates remain unchanged. The trend also affects new homebuyers and sellers in the local market. Real estate professionals and economists track property value trends as indicators of economic health and housing market conditions. The sustained four-year slowdown suggests structural factors are affecting the county's real estate market differently than other parts of Florida.

cards.teaser: Brightline rail service continues to affect Fort Pierce and Treasure Coast communities, with both challenges and benefits emerging from the high-speed rail line.

Local officials and residents are recognizing the holiday with events and observances. The combination of transportation infrastructure changes and cultural celebrations reflects the evolving character of Fort Pierce and the broader Treasure Coast. Community leaders continue to assess how Brightline service affects daily life while working to maximize benefits and minimize disruptions for residents.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce woman loses home and irreplaceable photos of late son after lightning strike
cards.teaser: Rosa Rivera returned home from church last month to find her Fort Pierce house destroyed by fire after a lightning strike. She lost photos of her late son and remains displaced with no insurance.
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce woman is displaced and calling for help after a lightning strike tore through her home last month, leaving her with broken windows, heavy damage, and almost nothing left. Rosa Rivera returned home from getting a haircut at church when a utility worker stopped her outside. The worker informed her that her house appeared to be on fire. St. Lucie County District Firefighters rushed to put out the flames. Rivera was told a lightning strike caused the fire.

Walking into her damaged home left Rivera stunned. She lost clothes, furniture and irreplaceable personal belongings including photos of her late son. Rivera's son passed away three years ago, making the loss of his photographs particularly devastating. The damage left Rivera displaced. She is uninsured and is now staying at her nephew's home while she rebuilds. Rivera, who is also disabled, was recovering from neck fusion surgery the same week she lost her home.

A memorial outside the damaged home is one of the few things Rivera has left that cannot be replaced. Despite everything, Rivera expressed gratitude for her nephew providing her a place to stay. She described the situation as overwhelming as she faces the challenges of being disabled, recovering from surgery, and losing her home all at once.

cards.headline: Jupiter makes history as 91 firefighters sworn in for town's first-ever fire department
cards.teaser: Jupiter officially launched Jupiter Fire Rescue on Monday at the Maltz Jupiter Theatre, swearing in 91 firefighters for the town's first fire department in its history.
cards.body:
For the first time in Jupiter history, the town has its own fire department. Ninety-one firefighters and their families gathered at the Maltz Jupiter Theatre on Monday as Jupiter officially launched Jupiter Fire Rescue, and its newest members took their oath of service. For Fire Chief Darrel Donatto, the ceremony marked the culmination of more than two years of work building a department from the ground up. Donatto called it the most proud day of his 45-year career in fire service, getting to swear in 91 new firefighters for the town of Jupiter.

Among the newest members of Jupiter Fire Rescue is Lieutenant Christian Lainhart, a sixth-generation Jupiter resident. After years serving with Martin County Fire Rescue, he saw the chance to serve at home. Lainhart said his roots are his responsibility, and the character embedded in him by his community can now be delivered back to the citizens of the community where he was born and raised. His wife, Jessica Lainhart, also grew up in Jupiter and watched her husband become one of the first firefighters in the town's history.

Behind every firefighter is a family making sacrifices of their own. The Lainharts acknowledged that there have been many Christmases and Thanksgivings where Christian has been working, reflecting the commitment required of firefighters and their families. The establishment of Jupiter Fire Rescue marks a significant milestone for the town as it takes control of its own fire and rescue services.

cards.headline: Loxahatchee residents celebrate completion of new levee 15 years after Tropical Storm Isaac floods
cards.teaser: Nearly fifteen years after Tropical Storm Isaac flooded North Loxahatchee in 2012, a brand-new levee is finally complete after years of lobbying for the $10.4 million needed for Phase II.
cards.body:
Nearly fifteen years after devastating floods wrecked North Loxahatchee during Tropical Storm Isaac, a brand-new levee is finally complete, taller, wider, and safer than ever. The failed levee back in 2012 left homes underwater, roads impassable, and residents stranded for days. For people in the area, the memory is personal. Argue, with the Indian Trail Improvement District, remembers the uphill battle to secure funding for a critical upgrade. She told reporters that funding never got final budget approval, claiming lawmakers did not see the project as a priority.

In 2013, the state appropriated $4 million for Phase I, protecting mostly agricultural land. But the eastern portion, the section shielding neighborhoods, was left incomplete when funding dried up. It would take years of lobbying, partnerships, and persistence from multiple organizations, local and state officials, and residents to finally secure the $10.4 million needed for Phase II, which stretches in total over 5 miles and now completes the levee system.

Everett Mitchell still remembers watching from his front porch as the old levee collapsed during Isaac. Water poured into homes from his home south, trapping neighbors inside. Some escaped on boats and canoes. The completion of the new levee system provides long-awaited flood protection for residents who endured the catastrophic flooding more than a decade ago and have been waiting for the upgrade ever since.

cards.headline: Wellington school zone speed cameras issued over 21,000 tickets before shutting off for summer
cards.teaser: Wellington's 11 school zone speed cameras are turned off for summer break because current state law doesn't consider summer school a regularly scheduled education program, Village Manager Jim Barnes says.
cards.body:
Wellington installed speed cameras in 11 school zones last fall, but Village Manager Jim Barnes says they will not be active during summer break. The reason is that current state law does not consider summer school a regularly scheduled education program, which is required to trigger enforcement. Barnes explained that summer school at this point does not meet the definition of a regularly scheduled education program, so the cameras will not be active during the summer. However, Barnes hinted that if the cameras stay in place, summer enforcement might eventually happen.

Since the cameras were installed, Wellington residents have had strong opinions on both sides. Some see them as essential for child safety, while others question the village's true motives. Lauren Brody asked whether the goal is trying to keep students and parents safe or trying to give people tickets and give revenue to the village of Wellington. Despite the controversy, the cameras have been busy issuing citations.

Since September, the cameras have issued more than 21,000 tickets, with October being the peak month at 5,100 tickets. Barnes says the data proves the cameras work, and the village is seeing a considerable amount of speed reduction in school zones. The cameras will remain inactive until the fall when regular school sessions resume and enforcement can legally restart under current state law.

cards.headline: Palm Beach Gardens serves as World Cup training site for Portugal and England national teams
cards.teaser: Palm Beach Gardens became more than a spectator in this year's World Cup. The city is serving as a training base for tournament teams including Portugal and England at Gardens District Park.
cards.body:
Palm Beach Gardens became more than a spectator in this year's World Cup as the city is serving as a training base for some of the tournament's biggest teams, including Portugal and England. Gardens District Park, the city's premier soccer facility, was selected as a base camp after years of building a reputation among elite soccer organizations. Sports and Special Facilities Director Tim Ford said that over the last several years, this facility has earned quite a reputation.

Ford said the fields were completed in 2019 and quickly drew national attention. The U.S. Soccer Federation began using the site in 2020 and has since hosted dozens of national youth team training camps. This year, seven Major League Soccer teams used it as a training site. Word spread internationally after Real Madrid used the facility last year. Portugal then selected it as a base camp for this year's World Cup, and England will also stop by to acclimate to the weather as it prepares for some pre-tournament matches in Florida.

Once the last flag football game wrapped up at Gardens District Park in early May, the city's agronomy team got to work preparing the fields for Portugal's arrival. Director of Agronomy staff have worked to ensure the facility meets international standards for elite soccer competition. The selection of Palm Beach Gardens as a World Cup training site represents a significant achievement for the city and showcases the quality of its athletic facilities on an international stage.

hero.headline: North Miami man arrested after attempted armed kidnapping at Port St. Lucie church
hero.teaser: A 64-year-old man was arrested Sunday after allegedly attempting to kidnap a 74-year-old woman at gunpoint in a church parking lot on Southwest Prima Vista Boulevard.
hero.body:
Jose Tsu Zamora, 64, of North Miami faces multiple felony charges following an attempted kidnapping at First United Methodist Church on Southwest Prima Vista Boulevard Sunday morning. The Port St. Lucie Police Department responded to the incident around 10:49 a.m. after witnesses intervened to stop the attack.

According to police, Zamora approached the 74-year-old victim in the church parking lot despite an active injunction prohibiting any contact with her. Zamora previously had a romantic relationship with the victim. While armed with a handgun, Zamora grabbed the victim by her arms and attempted to force her into his vehicle against her will. Several witnesses saw the incident and immediately intervened. Two Good Samaritans confronted Zamora and ordered him to release the victim.

During the confrontation, Zamora displayed his firearm before retreating to his vehicle and fleeing the scene. Church surveillance footage captured portions of the encounter and corroborated witness statements, showing Zamora pursuing the victim across the parking lot. The Port St. Lucie Police Department arrested Zamora Sunday evening. He faces charges of attempted kidnapping, aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, and violation of an injunction.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce woman loses home, irreplaceable photos of late son in lightning strike fire
cards.teaser: Rosa Rivera returned home from church last month to find her Fort Pierce house destroyed by a lightning strike, leaving her displaced and without insurance.
cards.body:
Rosa Rivera of Fort Pierce is displaced and calling for help after a lightning strike tore through her home last month, leaving her with broken windows, heavy damage, and almost nothing left. When Rivera returned home from getting a haircut at church, a utility worker stopped her outside to warn her that her house appeared to be on fire. St. Lucie County District Firefighters rushed to put out the flames. Rivera was told a lightning strike caused the fire.

Walking into her damaged home left Rivera stunned. Rivera lost clothes, furniture and irreplaceable personal belongings including photos of her late son, who passed away three years ago. The damage left Rivera displaced. She is uninsured and is now staying at her nephew's home while she rebuilds. Rivera said she is truly grateful for her nephew because without him, she does not know where she would be.

Rivera, who is also disabled, was recovering from neck fusion surgery the same week she lost her home. Rivera said the situation is very overwhelming and it is a lot for her to deal with. A memorial outside the damaged home is one of the few things Rivera has left that cannot be replaced. Despite everything, Rivera is trying to rebuild her life after the devastating fire.

cards.headline: Second victim comes forward in St. Lucie County school bus driver molestation case
cards.teaser: A former St. Lucie County school bus driver faces an additional battery charge after a second victim came forward in an investigation into inappropriate conduct with children.
cards.body:
Edwin Garcia, 72, of Port St. Lucie was arrested on a new battery charge May 28 when a second victim came forward with additional information for investigators. This comes after his initial arrest March 6 on two counts of lewd and lascivious molestation of a victim under 12 years of age. Garcia worked as a school bus driver for St. Lucie County schools before his arrest.

The investigation began March 4 when a school resource deputy received a report that Garcia had allegedly asked a 9-year-old student to lift her dress while riding the school bus. During the preliminary investigation, deputies developed additional information suggesting Garcia may have made inappropriate comments to the child and possibly pinched her over her clothing in the pelvic area, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. The case was then referred to the Criminal Investigations Division, leading to Garcia's initial arrest two days later on March 6.

The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office continues to investigate the allegations and is encouraging anyone who may have been a victim or has additional information to come forward. Anyone with information related to this case can contact Detective Corporal Hunter Limb at 772-462-7300 or email the Sheriff's Office. The ongoing investigation aims to identify any additional victims who may have encountered Garcia during his time as a school bus driver.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie woman faces attempted murder, arson charges after setting bedroom door on fire with victim inside
cards.teaser: A Port St.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie woman is in custody on charges of attempted murder and arson after allegedly setting fire to a bedroom door while a 62-year-old woman was trapped inside the room Sunday night. Port St. Lucie Police Department officers responded to reports of a domestic disturbance and active house fire at around 9:05 p.m. in the 1500 block of Southeast Airoso Boulevard.

According to investigators, the victim first noticed smoke coming from underneath her bedroom door. When she opened it, she discovered Michelle Picard, 26, standing nearby. The victim attempted to retrieve a fire extinguisher, but Picard allegedly physically attacked her and tried to prevent her from putting out the fire. Police say Picard made threatening statements and attempted to push the victim toward the flames.

The victim managed to escape to a bathroom, lock the door, and call 911. During the emergency call, Picard could be heard banging on the bathroom door in the background. Officers arrived to find flames inside the residence and immediately worked to evacuate everyone safely. They found Picard outside the residence and detained her.

Picard resisted arrest, causing injuries to one officer's leg and requiring another officer to be taken to a local hospital. The Port St. Lucie Police Department continues to investigate the incident. The charges against Picard include attempted murder, arson, battery on a law enforcement officer, and resisting arrest with violence.
